topics.label: Introduction to the cancer therapy lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives for cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional primary modalities of cancer treatment, detailing how surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy work alongside their clinical limitations.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer-specific biological vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic approaches that target intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, resistance mechanisms, and drug addiction
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogenic driver kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and examine the molecular mechanisms leading to drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the design and therapeutic mechanisms of unconjugated monoclonal antibodies and cytotoxic antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor surface antigens.

topics.label: Tumor immune surveillance and cellular immunotherapy strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of the immune system in recognizing tumors and examine immunotherapy modalities including checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic progress, ongoing challenges, and future directions in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess historical improvements in cancer outcomes, modern management challenges such as heterogeneity and toxicity, and future ethical and clinical directions.
